key_facts: The company ended the year with more than $1.5 billion of premium now in force.
The company was impacted by Hurricane Sally, PCS, Zeta, and Eta in 2020, with minimal exposure to Hurricane Delta and the Midwest Derecho.
The company had over 10,000 claims in the fourth quarter from named 2020 storms and other PCS events.
The company had no exposure to Hurricane Laura, Texas, Louisiana weather, or West Coast wildfires.
The company increased primary rates in Florida by close to 20% for the full year, including 7% in the fourth quarter.
The company continued geographic expansion efforts in 2020 and implemented catastrophe rapid response teams during the COVID-19 pandemic.
The company ended 2020 with total revenue up 14.2% to $1.1 billion, driven by growth in net premiums earned, realized gains on investments, and increases in service revenue.
The company's GAAP EPS for the quarter was a loss of $0.57, and non-GAAP adjusted EPS was a loss of $0.84.
The company's GAAP EPS for the year was $0.60, and non-GAAP adjusted EPS was a loss of $0.90.
The company's direct premiums written grew by 21.9% in Q4 and 7% for the full year, led by rate increases and increased volume.
The company's combined ratio decreased 18.9 points for the quarter to 124% but increased 9.7 points for the full year to 113.6%.
The full year increase in the combined ratio was driven by an increase of 13 points for increased weather in 2020.
The company's net investment income decreased 62.7% for the quarter and 33.7% for the full year due to lower yields on cash and fixed income investments.
The company repurchased approximately 193,000 shares at an aggregate cost of $2.4 million in the fourth quarter and 1.6 million shares at an aggregate cost of $28.9 million for the full year.
For 2021 guidance, the company expects a GAAP and non-GAAP adjusted earnings per share range of between $2.75 and $3, assuming no extraordinary weather events.

The 2021 guidance assumes a flat equity market for GAAP earnings per share, and if weather events exceed plan, the company expects a benefit from its claims adjusting business and increased loss cost.
